questions.q: State the formula for integration by parts.
questions.answer: Derived from the product rule: $\frac{d}{dx}(uv) = u'v + uv' \Rightarrow \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du$.
$u = x, dv = e^{2x}dx \Rightarrow du = dx, v = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x}$. $\int x e^{2x}dx = \frac{1}{2}x e^{2x} - \frac{1}{2}\int e^{2x}dx = \frac{1}{2}x e^{2x} - \frac{1}{4}e^{2x} + C$.
$u = x, dv = \sin x dx \Rightarrow du = dx, v = -\cos x$. $uv - \int v\,du = -x\cos x - \int(-\cos x)dx = -x\cos x + \sin x + C$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Logarithmic and Inverse Trig Integrands

questions.answer: $u = \ln x, dv = dx \Rightarrow du = \frac{1}{x}dx, v = x$. $x\ln x - \int x\cdot\frac{1}{x}dx = x\ln x - x + C$.
$u = \arctan x, dv = dx \Rightarrow du = \frac{dx}{1+x^2}, v = x$. $x\arctan x - \int \frac{x}{1+x^2}dx = x\arctan x - \frac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2) + C$.
$u = \ln x, dv = x dx \Rightarrow du = \frac{dx}{x}, v = \frac{x^2}{2}$. $\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x - \int \frac{x}{2}dx = \frac{x^2}{2}\ln x - \frac{x^2}{4} + C$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Repeated Integration and Tabular Method

questions.answer: Tabular: $D: x^2, 2x, 2, 0$; $I: \cos x, \sin x, -\cos x, -\sin x$. Pair with signs: $x^2\sin x - 2x(-\cos x) + 2(-\sin x) = x^2\sin x + 2x\cos x - 2\sin x + C$.

Tabular antiderivative: $e^{2x}\left(\frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{2x}{4} + \frac{2}{8}\right) = e^{2x}\left(\frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x}{2} + \frac{1}{4}\right)$. At $x=1$: $e^2(1/2 - 1/2 + 1/4) = \frac{e^2}{4}$. At $x=0$: $1(1/4) = 1/4$. Difference $= \frac{e^2 - 1}{4}$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Looping / Cyclic Integrals and Definite Bounds

questions.answer: Let $I = \int e^x\cos x dx$. By parts twice: $I = e^x\sin x + e^x\cos x - I \Rightarrow 2I = e^x(\sin x + \cos x) \Rightarrow I = \frac{1}{2}e^x(\sin x + \cos x) + C$.
